title: Great Jin
capsule: The Jin dynasty (金, 'gold') was founded in 1115 by Wanyan Aguda of the Jurchen Wanyan clan after he rebelled against the Liao dynasty in Manchuria and declared himself emperor. The Jin rapidly expanded, destroying the Liao in 1125 in alliance with Song China, then turning on Song and capturing the Northern Song capitals of Bianjing and taking Emperor Huizong prisoner in 1127, confining Song rule to the south. At its 12th-century apex the Jin governed northern China, Manchuria, and parts of Mongolia, with a population estimated at 53 million in 1186, and the dynasty presided over a rich Sinicized court culture. Mongol invasions beginning in 1211 under Genghis Khan steadily dismembered Jin territory, and in 1234 the last Jin emperor Aizong died as the combined Mongol-Song forces took the final capital Caizhou.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory is well-documented from Jin administrative records and Chinese historiography; the Mongol-period frontier zones are less precisely fixed in the dataset geometry and may be somewhat approximate.
